subject: radiology
title: Doppler Shift, Colour and Spectral Doppler, Elastography

steps.title: Doppler shift measures blood velocity
steps.tx: **Doppler shift** is the frequency change between transmitted sound and the echo returning from moving red cells. Flow toward the probe raises the returning frequency and flow away lowers it. The shift doubles when the beam meets flow head on and falls to zero at ninety degrees, which is why velocity readings demand an angle of sixty degrees or less with angle correction switched on.

steps.title: Colour Doppler maps direction
steps.tx: **Colour Doppler** paints mean velocity and direction over the grey scale image, by convention red toward the probe and blue away from it. The mnemonic BART, blue away red toward, holds only for the default map and flips if the operator inverts the scale. A tight carotid stenosis shows a mosaic of mixed colours where fast turbulent flow wraps through several hues inside one pixel cluster.

steps.title: Spectral Doppler waveforms
steps.tx: **Spectral Doppler** plots velocity against time inside a small sample gate, exposing the waveform shape that colour alone cannot show. Arteries supplying low resistance beds like brain, liver and kidney keep forward diastolic flow, while fasting limb arteries turn triphasic with a brief reversal. A tardus parvus waveform, slow rise with low peak, marks stenosis upstream of the sampled segment.

steps.title: Resistive index
steps.tx: **Resistive index** equals peak systolic velocity minus end diastolic velocity, divided by peak systolic velocity. Normal intrarenal values sit below 0.70, and a raised index appears in obstruction, rejection and medical renal disease without separating them alone. In the transplant kidney a value above 0.80 prompts a search for rejection, vein thrombosis or a tight arterial anastomosis rather than naming one cause.

steps.title: Aliasing on Doppler
steps.tx: **Aliasing** wraps the colour or spectral display when velocity exceeds the Nyquist limit, which is half the pulse repetition frequency. Fast flow through a stenotic aortic valve folds from the top of the scale to the bottom, faking reversed flow. Raising the scale, shifting the baseline, lowering probe frequency or switching to continuous wave Doppler, which has no Nyquist limit, unwraps the true peak.

steps.title: Elastography measures stiffness
steps.tx: **Elastography** estimates tissue stiffness either by tracking how a push deforms tissue or by timing shear waves crossing it. Shear wave speed rises in fibrosis, so liver readings climb from near 5 kilopascals in health toward 12.5 and beyond in cirrhosis, guiding biopsy and variceal screening decisions. A stiff breast mass raises concern, while a soft lesion of equal grey scale appearance favours a benign cause.

steps.title: Endoscopic and contrast ultrasound
steps.tx: **Endoscopic ultrasound** places a high frequency probe inside the gut lumen, millimetres from the pancreas, bile duct and gut wall layers. It stages oesophageal and rectal tumours by wall layer invasion and guides needle sampling of pancreatic masses through the stomach wall. Contrast enhanced ultrasound instead uses intravenous microbubbles to show liver lesion washout in real time without radiation or kidney injury.

steps.title: Mirror artefact in Doppler
steps.tx: **Mirror artefact** also corrupts Doppler studies when a strong reflector like the diaphragm or bladder wall folds a vessel image into a false second location. Spectral traces from the ghost vessel duplicate the real waveform, tempting a report of two arteries where one exists. Changing the acoustic window, reducing gain and tracing the vessel in two planes exposes the copy before measurements are recorded.
